questions.md:
Find the current through the $3\,\Omega$ resistor in the figure using the superposition theorem.

*A $5\text{ A}$ current source in parallel with a $5\,\Omega + 10\,\Omega$ branch; $2\,\Omega$ series to a $3\,\Omega + 4\,\Omega$ branch; a $20\text{ V}$ source is connected across the $4\,\Omega$ resistor.*

Determine the current $I_x$ in the circuit shown using the superposition theorem.

*$20\text{ V}$ source, $5\,\Omega$ (current $I_x$) to a node; $30\text{ A}$ source from the node to ground; $1\,\Omega$ to a dependent voltage source $4I_x$.*

Find the current through the $1\,\Omega$ resistor using the superposition theorem in the network shown.

*$4\text{ V}$ source, $2\,\Omega$ to a middle node, $1\,\Omega$ from the middle node to ground, $3\,\Omega$ to the right node, $3\text{ A}$ source into the right node, $1\text{ A}$ source from the left top node to the right node.*

In the network shown in the figure, the switch is moved from position 1 to 2 at $t = 0$. The switch was in position 1 for a long time. Determine the expression for the current $i(t)$.

*Series loop: switch (position 1 to a $20\text{ V}$ source, position 2 to a $50\text{ V}$ source), $10\,\Omega$, $2\text{ H}$, $3\text{ F}$.*

Obtain the complete response $v$ and then $i$ for $t > 0$ in the circuit shown in the figure (assume the circuit is initially unenergized).

*$2\text{ A}$ source in the middle branch, shorted by a switch that opens at $t=0$; left branch $10\,\Omega$ + $\tfrac{1}{20}\text{ F}$ (voltage $v$); right branch $4\,\Omega$ + $2\text{ H}$ (current $i$).*

In the network shown in the figure, at $t = 0$ switch 1 is closed, and switch 2 is closed 4 seconds later. Find $i(t)$ for $t > 0$. (Assume the inductor has zero initial current.)

*$40\text{ V}$ source, $4\,\Omega$, switch $S_1$ to node P; from P: switch $S_2$ ($t=4$) with $2\,\Omega$ and $10\text{ V}$ to ground; $6\,\Omega$ and $5\text{ H}$ (current $i$) to ground.*

In the network shown in the figure, a steady state is reached with the switch open. At $t = 0$, the switch is closed. Find the three loop currents at $t = 0^+$.

*$6\text{ V}$ source, $2\,\Omega$ series; then $4\,\Omega$ over $1\text{ H}$ in one branch, $0.5\text{ F}$ over $1\text{ F}$ in parallel; the switch joins the midpoints of the two branches. Loop currents $i_1, i_2, i_3$.*

In the network of the figure, the switch is closed at $t = 0$. With the capacitor uncharged, find the values of $i$ and $\dfrac{di}{dt}$ at $t = 0^+$.

*Series circuit: $100\text{ V}$ source, switch, $1000\,\Omega$, $1\,\mu\text{F}$.*

In the network shown in the figure, calculate
(a) $i_L(0^+)$, $v_C(0^+)$, $v_R(0^+)$
(b) $\dfrac{di_L}{dt}(0^+)$, $\dfrac{dv_C}{dt}(0^+)$, $\dfrac{dv_R}{dt}(0^+)$
(c) $i_L(\infty)$, $v_C(\infty)$, $v_R(\infty)$.

*$3u(t)\text{ A}$ source, $2\,\Omega$ shunt ($v_R$), series $4\,\Omega$, shunt $\tfrac12\text{ F}$ ($v_C$) with a $20\text{ V}$ source, shunt $0.6\text{ H}$ ($i_L$).*

In the network of the figure, the switch is closed and a steady state is attained. At $t = 0$, the switch is opened. Determine the current through the inductor using the Laplace transform.

*$5\text{ V}$ source, switch, $2.5\,\Omega$, then $200\,\mu\text{F}$ in parallel with $0.5\text{ H}$.*

The switch in the network shown in the figure is closed at $t = 0$. Determine the voltage across the capacitor using the Laplace transform.

*$10\text{ V}$ source, switch, $10\,\Omega$ series, then $10\,\Omega$ in parallel with $2\text{ F}$ ($v_c(t)$).*

In the network shown in the figure, the switch is opened at $t = 0$. Steady-state condition is achieved before $t = 0$. Using the Laplace transform, calculate $i(t)$.

*$1\text{ V}$ source and switch feeding a $1\text{ F}$ capacitor; in parallel with the capacitor, $0.5\text{ H}$ in series with $1\,\Omega$ carrying $i(t)$.*

The square wave shown in the figure (switching between $200\text{ V}$ and $300\text{ V}$, each level lasting $T$) is fed to an RC integrating circuit. Compute and plot the output waveform under steady-state conditions if $RC = 2.5T$.

A symmetrical square wave of amplitude $\pm 5\text{ V}$ and frequency $2\text{ kHz}$ is impressed on a low-pass RC circuit. If $R = 5\text{ k}\Omega$ and $C = 0.1\,\mu\text{F}$, calculate and plot the steady-state output with respect to time.

A symmetrical square wave whose peak-to-peak amplitude is $2\text{ V}$ and whose average value is zero is applied to an RC integrating circuit. The time constant of the circuit is equal to half the period of the square wave. Find the peak-to-peak value of the output amplitude.
